pillar_reactions.evidence: He interrupted to ask 'Does the workout include stretching or not?', then volunteered the strongest buying statement of the call and tied it directly to why this is worth paying for: 'Mobility is a must for me. This is the reason why, because there's a lot of workouts out there, and there's a lot of information right there right now that you could do for free these days. But between other things, based on motivation and having that professional trainer, mobility is something that you don't find much.' He then pictured himself doing it — 'I probably got to start with a five-pounder' — and the rep normalised that well.

Presented as the what/when/how-much frame, cutting the sodas, whole foods, no chicken-and-rice, producing a small deficit while protein stays high so muscle is preserved. He had already conceded the sugar problem earlier and agreed to change it ('I tried. I used to do it every day. Now I'm only on weekends'). Response to the pillar check was a short affirmative with no questions and no pushback.

Delivered as the most important pillar and aimed squarely at his stated gap — Trevor plans around his life, personal number, schedules changed when tax season hits, filmed workouts with form feedback, teach-a-man-to-fish. He confirmed understanding rather than excitement: 'so far it's good, so far I understand how it works.' Asked what would be missing he re-listed his own criteria — 'It's usually nutrition, the right instruction, and the right motivation' — and then flagged a positive surprise: 'maybe that Thursday Live, it could probably help also, I wasn't thinking that there was any live.' Given accountability is precisely what he has been missing for six years, this drew less reaction than it should have.

anchors.raw: we're both accountants, so we are very, very meticulous about, you know, the dollar, right, so we have kids, it's a family, we have a couple of mortgages, we have to make sure that we cover, so popping out a thousand dollars a month, whatever it is, it's a bill, so we just have to make sure that the bill is something that we could cover.
anchors.note: The decisive anchor. Two professional accountants who evaluate this as a recurring line item against multiple mortgages, not as a discretionary purchase. It reframes $1,000/month from an investment into a bill that must be underwritten, and it means the decision genuinely is joint — which makes the standard 'this isn't a joint decision' spouse play unusable here.

anchors.raw: I just thought, you know, the numbers is a little high for what I was expecting to tell the truth.
anchors.note: He came in with a lower number in his head, having found Trevor only the previous night. No pre-framing of price had been done by the setter, so $6,000 landed cold roughly 24 hours after first contact.

anchors.raw: She even told me, she goes, why don't you use that row or whatever, you know, you lose weight like in a month, you lose those 10 pounds. You can easily do
anchors.competitor: a rowing machine / quick weight-loss shortcut suggested by his wife
anchors.note: The person whose approval the purchase requires has already proposed a free alternative that reaches his stated headline goal of losing 10-15 pounds. He rejected it himself as a gimmick and articulated why — losing weight without training costs muscle — but the rep never armed him with that argument to take into the conversation that night. The rep did explain the biology, which helps, but it was never framed as 'here is what to tell her'.

anchors.raw: there's a lot of workouts out there, you know, and there's a lot of information right there right now that you could do for free these days
anchors.competitor: free online workout content and workout apps he has used before
anchors.note: He raised the free alternative and defeated it himself in the same breath — motivation, professional instruction and mobility are what free content does not give him. That is the ideal outcome for this anchor, and it came from the rep's earlier P4f question about why he does not just follow videos online. Worth keeping as evidence that the question works.

anchors.raw: it seemed to me it would be more expensive and definitely more difficult to find one person that would do that
anchors.note: He assessed the nearest comparable service as costlier and impractical, and dismissed it before price was mentioned. A rare supportive anchor that the rep did not exploit at the close — this was the frame to return to when $6,000 landed high.

anchors.raw: I'm putting a room together in the next couple of months for our own gym type of in the basement
anchors.note: He is already committing capital to a home gym and buys creatine, whey and vitamins. There is real intent-backed spend here, which sits awkwardly against 'we're full of bills' and suggests the constraint is joint approval and framing more than absolute capacity.

anchors.raw: it's nothing but a reel and a conversation and going in. To a $3,000 $6,000 deal almost immediately
anchors.note: Time-to-decision is the anchor here rather than a competing number. He first saw Trevor the previous night and is being asked for thousands the next day, with no proof asset available beyond an Instagram feed. Note he says '$3,000 $6,000', suggesting he had heard or assumed a lower figure at some point.

unmet_demand.want: Something concrete to look at that shows what the programme actually is before committing thousands — sample programming, structured results, anything beyond a short reel
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The honest answer given was that it does not exist: 'to answer the program aspects, there is not much more.' The rep fell back to screensharing Trevor's Instagram and client DMs and citing 1,000+ clients, then promised to send the link. For a prospect one day from first contact this is a real gap in sales collateral rather than in the coaching product itself — the substance exists, nothing packages it.

unmet_demand.want: An instalment plan he can actually afford — he named $1,000/month as his ceiling
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The plan as quoted adds roughly $200 per payment, landing at $1,200/month for either term, which is above the ceiling he had just stated. There is a genuine commercial gap between the price of flexibility and what this buyer can carry, and the terms were also stated inconsistently enough that he had to challenge them.

unmet_demand.want: Confirmation that kettlebell training can be programmed around a chronic lower back that rules out deadlifts
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He named the constraint clearly and it was never addressed. The presentation instead promised a mobility routine tailored to his lower back, without anyone establishing whether the loaded hip-hinge movements at the core of kettlebell work are appropriate. Probably solvable by a competent coach, but unverified on the call and a genuine risk for a 56-year-old with a twenty-year back history.

unmet_demand.want: A path back to recreational boxing once strength and agility return
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He named it as a real goal and deferred it himself for fear of losing muscle mass at his age. Nobody said whether the programme supports or conflicts with that, so the motivational hook went unused and the question is unanswered.

unmet_demand.want: Training that survives three months of 14-hour days during tax season
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep addressed it directly and credibly — schedules changed on communication, sessions dropped to 20-30 minutes, other clients run businesses — so this is served in principle. It is listed here only because it is the make-or-break requirement for this specific buyer and nothing concrete was committed to, such as what a February week actually looks like.
